newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul allows institutions to raise funds abroad.
newsitem.headline: Seoul allows institutions to raise funds abroad.

text.p: The South Korean government will allow local financial institutions to raise about $200 million each in Asia and in Europe to launch funds specialising in investment in the domestic bond market this year, a finance ministry official said on Monday.
No other details were given but the measure was part of the Seoul government's attempt to support the won by encouraging inflows of foreign funds.
A $100 million fund was launched last October by raising money in Europe for similar purposes.
At present, foreigners are only allowed to invest in non-guaranteed convertible bonds issued by small and medium-sized companies.
